Listen to this article Share Moniepoint is restructuring its engineering and product operations as the fintech expands its financial services business, which processes more than $400 billion in annual digital payment transaction value across its subsidiaries. The restructuring will introduce a platform-based operating model built around smaller, focused teams responsible for developing and managing products from end to end. The company said the changes are intended to improve engineering efficiency, accelerate product development, strengthen operational reliability and support expansion into new markets. In a holding statement, Moniepoint said its organisational structure must evolve as the business grows from a single product into a group of financial services businesses serving merchants, businesses and individual customers. Read also: Moniepoint bets on transaction data to bridge Nigeria’s SME credit gap The new model will organise teams into platform groups, with each group responsible for specific product areas. The structure is designed to give teams greater autonomy and clearer accountability while improving coordination between product development and the underlying technology infrastructure. A central feature of the restructuring is the introduction of platform architects, who will design and oversee the technical systems supporting each platform group. These roles will form part of Moniepoint’s broader Product Operating Model and architectural governance framework, which guide the development of solutions, platform capabilities and technical foundations. The shift comes as the company seeks to manage the growing complexity of its technology operations while maintaining the reliability and consistency of services used by businesses and individuals. Moniepoint’s financial services include payments, banking, credit and business management solutions. Its technology enables merchants to accept payments, manage cash flow and access business tools, while providing individuals with everyday banking services. The company has built a significant presence in Nigeria’s informal economy, supported by an agent network covering all 774 local government areas. It is also expanding its operations in Kenya, increasing the need for technology systems capable of supporting a broader customer base and operations across markets. The company said its proprietary technology, developed in-house over the past decade, has been central to its growth and its ability to serve the realities of African commerce. As the business expands, the platform-based structure is expected to strengthen ownership of products throughout their development and operation, rather than separating responsibility across multiple teams. Moniepoint said this approach should enable faster product development, improve operational performance and deliver more consistent services to customers. The restructuring will also change some existing roles, while creating new positions to support the revised operating model. The company said it would consider employees whose current roles are affected for available positions elsewhere in the business where suitable opportunities exist. Moniepoint’s move reflects the operational demands of scaling a financial technology business whose services depend on the continuous performance of payment systems, banking infrastructure and business applications. With annual digital payment transaction value exceeding $400 billion, the company’s ability to maintain reliable technology while expanding its product range and geographic reach is increasingly central to its growth strategy. The restructuring is intended to align its engineering and product functions with that next phase of expansion, placing greater emphasis on platform ownership, technical governance and operational efficiency as Moniepoint develops its financial services business across Africa.
